---
title: "Get started"
---

This page takes you from an empty directory to a plugin project that passes its first `benchweave-sdk check`. Each step gives the command to run, the output you should see, and a link for the output you did not see. The commands work on Linux, macOS and Windows.

You need Python 3.13 or later and the `uv` package tool. You do not need a BenchWeave gateway. You do not need hardware. All commands run offline after the installs.

## Step 0. Prepare an environment

Install `uv` first. The [uv installation guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) explains the options. The usual commands are:

```text
# macOS and Linux
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
# Windows PowerShell
powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
```

Make a project directory and create a virtual environment in it:

```sh
mkdir first-plugin
cd first-plugin
uv venv
```

You should see a line that ends with `Activate with: source .venv/bin/activate`.

Activate the environment. Run the line for your operating system:

```sh
# macOS and Linux
source .venv/bin/activate
# Windows PowerShell
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
# Windows cmd
.venv\Scripts\activate.bat
```

If the activation line does not appear, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd).

## Step 1. Install the SDK

Install the SDK with the scaffold extra. The `new` command in Step 2 needs this extra:

```sh
uv pip install 'benchweave-sdk[scaffold]'
```

You should see `Installed` lines, and one of them names `benchweave-sdk`.

Verify the install:

```sh
benchweave-sdk --version
```

You should see the tool name and a version number, with no error.

If the install stops with a no-virtual-environment error, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd).

## Step 2. Generate a plugin project

> [!CAUTION]
> A generated project is not qualified firmware and not a real instrument driver. The protocol and the test data are synthetic placeholders.

Generate a synthetic plugin project:

```sh
benchweave-sdk new plugins/acme/model100 --package benchweave_acme_model100
```

You should see this message:

```text
Created synthetic plugin at <your-path>/plugins/acme/model100;
review before hardware or publication.
```

The path in the message is the real path of your directory. On macOS, a path that you reach through `/tmp` is reported as `/private/tmp`. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd) for this behavior.

The project contains these files, and the steps below use each of them:

```text
plugins/acme/model100/
├── pyproject.toml                     # build configuration and test dependencies
├── AI-GUIDE.md                        # the development workflow
├── CLAUDE.md                          # agent notes; imports the SDK-managed guide
├── AGENTS.md                          # SDK-managed agent guide
├── .claude/skills/                    # SDK-managed workflow skills
├── src/benchweave_acme_model100/      # the import package
│   ├── adapter.py                     # the SDK-facing adapter
│   ├── protocol.py                    # the synthetic device protocol
│   └── descriptor.json                # the device and operation contract
└── tests/                             # the generated tests
```

The generated tree holds more files than this diagram. The [plugin developer guide](plugin-sdk.qmd) lists the complete tree.

## Step 3. Install the project and run its tests

Change into the project. Install it with its test dependencies. Run the tests:

```sh
cd plugins/acme/model100
uv pip install -e '.[test]'
pytest
```

The last summary line contains the word `passed`. The number of tests grows when the scaffold grows, so this page does not state a number.

If `pytest` reports `ModuleNotFoundError` for a package, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd).

## Step 4. Run the descriptor check

Run the offline descriptor check:

```sh
benchweave-sdk check src/benchweave_acme_model100/descriptor.json
```

You should see this message:

```text
Descriptor schema and basic S01/S02/S04 checks passed; full conformance and
hardware evidence remain separate.
```

This message is the first check-pass. A pass exits with code 0. A failure exits with a nonzero code and an error message.

A pass means the descriptor matches the vendored schema and the basic checks. It does not mean that the plugin is conformant, admitted to a gateway, or qualified for hardware. The [plugin developer guide](plugin-sdk.qmd) explains the full scope. You do not need the S01–S18, C01–C12 and M01–M14 obligations to reach this pass. The [Glossary](glossary.qmd) explains these families.

If the check fails, the message names the file and the reason. Correct the descriptor, then run the command again.

## Step 5. Build and inventory

Build the project:

```sh
uv build
```

You should see two `Successfully built` lines. The `dist/` directory now holds a wheel and a source archive.

Print the inventory of the prepared bundle:

```sh
benchweave-sdk inventory dist/
```

You should see JSON output. Each row carries the keys `path`, `bytes` and `sha256`. There is one row for each file under `dist/`.

If inventory reports a missing argument, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd).

## Step 6. Check the scaffold pin

Check that the project's pinned SDK version matches the installed SDK:

```sh
benchweave-sdk doctor
```

You should see a line that starts with `Scaffold version matches the installed SDK:`. The line ends with the installed SDK version.

If doctor reports a mismatch, the project's pinned SDK version and the installed one differ. Align the pin with the SDK you use, then run the command again.

## Step 7. Where next

- Replace the synthetic protocol with verified device behavior. Start with prompt 2 in `AI-GUIDE.md`.
- A user interface is optional. The section below generates a second project with a UI and checks it.
- Two copies of the SDK exist. [Which checkout](which-checkout.qmd) tells you which one to use.
- Terms with one fixed meaning live in the [Glossary](glossary.qmd).
- The full depth lives in the [plugin developer guide](plugin-sdk.qmd).
- The release commands are `benchweave-sdk package` and `benchweave-sdk submit`. The registry documentation owns their walkthrough. You do not need them to reach the first check-pass.
- Record the applicable S01–S18, C01–C12 and M01–M14 obligations before a release. None of them block the first check-pass.

## Optional. Check a project with a UI

Generate a second project with presentation resources. Return to the `first-plugin` directory first:

```sh
cd ../..
benchweave-sdk new plugins/acme/model200 --package benchweave_acme_model200 --with-ui
cd plugins/acme/model200
benchweave-sdk check-ui src/benchweave_acme_model200/presentation.json \
  --descriptor src/benchweave_acme_model200/descriptor.json \
  --resources src/benchweave_acme_model200 \
  --catalogue src/benchweave_acme_model200/binding-catalogue.json \
  --firmware 1.0.0
```

You should see this message:

```text
Offline presentation checks passed; not admission or approval to apply settings.
```

The `--firmware` value comes from the generated project. The descriptor's `identity.supported_firmware` list declares it. When you write your own descriptor, use a value from your own list.

> [!CAUTION]
> A preview pass is not admission, not approval to apply settings, and not hardware qualification.

Preview the pages in a browser. The preview serves this project's pages on the standalone host, on the scripted mock transport. The preview command needs the server extra. Install the extra once, in the environment you made in Step 1:

```text
uv pip install 'benchweave-sdk[server]'
benchweave-sdk preview-ui . --no-open
```

The preview serves until you stop it. Press `Ctrl+C` to stop the server. With `--no-open`, open the printed URL in a browser yourself. The startup output also prints a bearer token. The token gates REST mutations and MCP over HTTP. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd) for the stop behavior.
